﴿When we have died…﴾ al-Akhfash said: this statement is in the form of a response, as if it had been said to them: "You will be returned," and they said: "When we have died and become dust?" Others said: the meaning of the sentence is: "Qaf, by the Qur'an, they will certainly be resurrected," and so they said: "When we have died and become dust?" The meaning is: "Will we be resurrected when we are in that state?" Ibn Jarir said: when they marveled at Allah's threat against them for denying Muhammad ﷺ, and they said: "This is a strange thing," it was as if He said to them: "You will know when you are resurrected what your state will be for denying Muhammad," and so they said: "When we have died and become dust?!"

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿That is a far return﴾, meaning: a return to life that is "far." Ibn Qutaybah said: meaning, it will not happen.

﴿We already know what the earth takes away of them﴾, meaning: what the earth consumes of their flesh, their blood and their hair once they die. He means that this is not hidden from His knowledge. ﴿And with Us is a preserved record﴾, meaning: along with Our knowledge of that, there is a record that preserves their number, their names, and what the earth takes away of them. It is the Preserved Tablet, in which everything that will happen has been recorded.

﴿But they denied the truth﴾, which is the Qur'an. "Al-Marij" means "the confused." Ibn Qutaybah said: it is said: "The affair of the people became confused (maraja)" and "the religion became confused," and the origin of this is that a thing becomes unsettled and does not remain still. It is said: "The ring became loose on my finger" when it became loose due to thinness. The exegetes said: the meaning of the confusion of their affair is that they would at one time call the Prophet ﷺ a sorcerer, at another a poet, and at another a teacher, and they would call the Qur'an at one time magic, at another fabricated, and at another a poem (rajaz). So their affair was ambiguous and confused for them. [p-7]

Then He pointed them to His power to resurrect by His saying: ﴿Have they not looked at the sky above them, how We built it and adorned it, with no cracks in it?﴾ "Without pillars," "and We adorned it" with the stars. ﴿And it has no fissures﴾, meaning no splits or cracks. The word *zawj* means a kind (*jins*). *Bahij* means beautiful, as said by Abu 'Ubayda. Ibn Qutayba said: *bahij* is that in which one takes delight.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿As an insight and a reminder for every servant who turns back [to Allah]﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: That is, We did this so that We might give insight and point to the power [of Allah]. *Munib* is one who returns to Allah and reflects on His power.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We send down from the sky water﴾, which is rain, ﴿blessed﴾, meaning abundant in good, in which is the life of everything, ﴿and We caused to grow by it gardens﴾, which are orchards, ﴿and the grain of the harvest﴾. He meant: the harvested grain, and He attributed it to itself, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, this is the true certainty﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 95], and His saying: ﴿From the jugular vein﴾ [Qaf: 16]. The jugular vein is the same as the vein. Just as one says *salat al-ula* (the first prayer) meaning the first prayer, and *masjid al-jami'* (the congregational mosque) meaning the congregational mosque, these things are attributed to themselves only because their names differ in wording. This is the view of al-Farra' and Ibn Qutayba. Others said: he meant the grain of the harvested plant. ﴿And palm trees﴾, meaning and We caused to grow the palm trees, ﴿tall﴾, and *busuquha* is their height. Ibn Qutayba said: it is said that a thing *basaqa* (grows tall) *yabsuqu busuqan* when it becomes tall. *Nadid* means piled one upon another, and that is before it opens. When it splits, its spathe dries and its pollen scatters, so it is no longer *nadid*.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿As provision for the servants﴾, meaning We caused these things to grow for provision. ﴿And We revived by it﴾, meaning by the rain, ﴿a dead land﴾. ﴿Thus will be the emergence﴾ from the graves.

Then He mentioned the nations that denied, after this, and its explanation has already preceded up to His saying: ﴿So My warning was justified﴾, meaning My punishment became due upon them.

Some scholars have related that the **Warid** is a vein spread throughout the body, mingling with all the organs. The meaning: "I was innocent of it." (p-١٥) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And his companion will say﴾. Muqatil said: he is his angel, the one who used to record his evil deeds in the worldly abode. He says to his Lord: "I have recorded what You entrusted me with. This is ready and present with me from his evil deed. I have brought it to You, with his deed." There are two views concerning "mā" (what). The first is that it means "man" (who), as said by Mujahid.

The second is that it means "thing" (shay'), so the sense is: "This is a thing ready with me." This was said by al-Zajjaj. We have already explained the meaning of "ʿatīd" (ready) in this surah [Qaf 50:18]. Then Allah, may He be exalted, says: ﴿Cast into Hell﴾. Concerning the address in this phrase there are three views.

The first is that it is an address to one person using the dual form of address. Al-Farra' said: The Arabs command one person or a group using the dual form. They say to a man, "Woe to you! Mount it and drive it," which I heard from the Arabs. Some of them recited to me:

"I said to my companion, 'Do not hold us back from plucking its roots, and cut down the wormwood.'"

Abu Tharwan also recited to me:

"If you two rebuke me, O son of ʿAffan, I will be rebuked; and if you two leave me, I will protect an inviolable honour."

We see that this comes from them, because the least number of helpers a man has with his camels and sheep is two, and likewise the least number of a company of travellers is three. So the speech was directed at his two companions. Do you not see that in poetry the most common expressions are "O my two companions" and "O my two friends"? Imru' al-Qays said:

"My two friends, pass by me at Umm Jundab, that we may satisfy the desires of the tormented heart."

Then he said:

"Did you not see that whenever I came to her at night, I found in her a fragrance, even if she had not perfumed herself."

He then returned to the singular, while his speech began in the dual. Muqatil went in this direction, and said: ﴿Cast﴾ is an address to the keeper, meaning the keeper of the Fire.

The second view is that it is a verb in the dual used for emphasis (taʾkīd, reinforcement). It is as if, when He said ﴿Cast﴾, it stood in place of "cast, cast." Likewise, "qifā nabki" (stop, let us weep) means "stop, stop." Since it stands in place of two verbs, it is in the dual. This was said by al-Mubarrad.

The third view is that it is a command to the two angels, meaning the driver and the witness. This is the preference of al-Zajjaj.

As for ﴿al-kaffār﴾ (the great disbeliever), it is more intensive in emphasis than "al-kāfir" (the disbeliever). And ﴿al-ʿanīd﴾ (the obstinate) we have explained in [Hud 11:59].

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Hinderer of good﴾. Regarding what is meant by "good" here, there are three views.

The first is the obligatory zakat, said by Qatadah.

The second is that it means Islam, that he prevents people from entering it. This was said by al-Dahhak and Muqatil, who mentioned that it was revealed concerning al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, who prevented his nephews from accepting Islam.

The third is that it is general, covering all good, whether in speech or action, as related by al-Mawardi.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿transgressor﴾, meaning a wrongdoer who does not affirm divine oneness (tawhid, the affirmation of Allah's oneness). ﴿doubter﴾, meaning one who is in doubt about the truth, from their saying "arāba al-rajul" (the man became one in doubt), when he became a person of doubt.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And his companion will say﴾. Concerning this there are two views.

The first is that it is his devil. This was said by Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, and the majority. In the speech there is an ellipsis; its sense is: the human claimed against his companion from the devils that it had misled him, (p-١٨) so he says: ﴿Our Lord, I did not make him transgress﴾, meaning I had no power to lead him astray by compulsion, and rather he transgressed by his own error.

The second is that it is the angel who used to record the evil deeds.

Then, concerning what the disbeliever claims against the angel, there are two views.

The first is that he says: "He added to me in what he recorded." So the angel says: "I did not make him transgress," meaning, "I did not add to what he did." This was said by Saʿid ibn Jubayr.

The second is that he says: "He used to hasten me away from repentance." So he says: "Our Lord, I did not make him transgress." This is the saying of al-Farra'.

The second is that it is their dispute with their companions who led them astray, said by Abu al-ʿAliyah. As for their disputing over the wrongs they committed among themselves in the world, that cannot be disregarded, because it is the Day of Equitable Judgment.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And I had already sent to you the warning﴾, meaning I had already informed you, through the tongues of the messengers, of My punishment in the Hereafter for those who disbelieve.

This is the saying of Ibn al-Sa'ib, the preference of al-Farra', and Ibn Qutaybah. Al-Zajjaj said: The accusative of "yawm" (day) has two possibilities. One is in the sense: the word will not be changed before Me on that day. The second is in the sense: and warn them of the Day We say to Hell.

As for the purpose of Allah asking it, though He knows whether it has been filled or not, it is a rebuke to those who were cast into it, an increase in their distress, and a proof of the truth of His saying: ﴿I will surely fill Hell﴾ [al-A'raf: 18]. Regarding its saying ﴿Is there any more?﴾ there are two opinions among the scholars of language.

(p-20) One is that it says this after it has become full, so the meaning is: Is there any place left in me that has not been filled? That is, I am already full.

The second is that it says this out of rage against those who disobeyed Allah, and Allah gave it the ability to discern and to speak, just as He gave the ant the ability to say: ﴿Enter your dwellings﴾ [al-Naml: 18], and gave created things the ability to glorify Him with His praise.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Paradise is brought near to the God-fearing﴾, that is, it is brought close to the God-fearing [from polytheism], ﴿not far off﴾, that is, it is placed to the right of the Throne, where the people of the Standing place can see it, and it will be said to them: "This is what you see," ﴿that which you were promised﴾. 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, Ibn 'Umar, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, and Ibn Muhaysin recited: "yu'adun" with a ya, ﴿for every one who turns often (to Allah)﴾. There are opinions concerning this, which we have mentioned in [al-Isra': 25]. Regarding ﴿who guards﴾ there are two opinions.

One is: the one who guards his sins until he turns away from them, said by Ibn 'Abbas.

The second is: the one who guards the command of Allah, said by Muqatil.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whoever feared the Most Merciful unseen﴾, we have explained it in [al-Anbiya': 49]. ﴿And comes with a heart turned in repentance﴾, that is, returning to obedience to Allah from disobedience to Him.

﴿Enter it﴾, that is, it will be said to them: Enter Paradise ﴿in peace﴾. That is because they were safe from the punishment of Allah, and they were safe therein from sorrows, change, and cessation, and Allah and His angels greet them. ﴿That is the Day of Eternity﴾ in Paradise, because there is no death in it and no cessation.

﴿For them is whatever they wish therein﴾. That is because they ask Allah until their requests are exhausted, (p-21) and they are given what they wished, then He increases them with what they did not ask for; this is His saying: ﴿And with Us is more⁠﴾. The commentators have three opinions about what is meant by this increase.

One: it is the gazing upon Allah, mighty and majestic. 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, related from the Prophet ﷺ regarding His saying: ﴿And with Us is more﴾, he said: "He will manifest Himself to them." Anas ibn Malik said regarding His saying: ﴿And with Us is more﴾: "The Lord, exalted is He, will manifest Himself to them every Friday."

The second: the cloud passes over the people of Paradise and rains down the Houris upon them, and the Houris say: "We are those of whom Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿And with Us is more﴾." Related by al-Zajjaj.

The third: the increase is beyond what they desired and asked for, of what no ear has heard and what has not occurred to the heart of any human being. Mentioned by Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi.

Then He warned the disbelievers of Makkah with what follows this, up to His saying: ﴿So they roamed through the lands﴾. The majority recited "fa-naqqabu" with a fatha on the nun and the qaf, with shaddah. As for "mahis" (escape), it is the way of deviation; we have fully explained its meaning in [al-Nisa': 121].

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed in that is a reminder﴾, meaning in what He has mentioned of the destruction of the towns, ﴿a reminder and an admonition﴾, that is, a remembrance and a lesson, ﴿for whoever has a heart﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: that is, intellect. Al-Farra' said: It is permissible in the language to say: "You have no heart," and "Your heart is not with you," meaning intellect. Ibn Qutaybah said: Since the heart is the place of the intellect, it is referred to by it. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is: for the one who turns his heart to understanding. ﴿Or gives ear﴾, that is, listens to Me, ﴿while he is a witness﴾, that is, while his heart is present in what he hears. Al-Farra' said: "while he is a witness" means present, not absent.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We certainly created the heavens and the earth﴾. The commentators mentioned that the Jews said: Allah created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, the last of which was Friday, and He rested on Saturday, therefore we do no work on it. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So be patient over what they say﴾, that is, over their slander and lies. The commentators said: the meaning of His saying ﴿So be patient﴾ was abrogated by the verse of the sword. ﴿And exalt with praise of your Lord﴾, that is, pray with praise of your Lord and declaring Him free from what the falsifiers say, ﴿before the rising of the sun﴾, which is the Fajr prayer, ﴿and before setting﴾. On this there are two opinions.

One: the Zuhr and 'Asr prayers, said by Ibn 'Abbas.

The second: the 'Asr prayer, said by Qatadah. Al-Bukhari and Muslim related in their Sahihs, from the hadith of Jarir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: "We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the night of the full moon, and he said: Indeed you will see your Lord plainly, just as you see this moon, and you will not be harmed in seeing Him. So if you are able not to be overcome in a prayer before the rising of the sun and before its setting, then do so." His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And during part of the night, glorify Him﴾. On this there are three opinions.

One: it is prayer during the whole night, at whatever time one prays in it, said by Mujahid.

The second: the 'Isha' prayer, said by Ibn Zayd.

The third: the Maghrib and 'Isha' prayers, said by Muqatil.

The second: it is the voluntary prayers after the obligatory ones, said by Ibn Zayd.

The third: it is glorification with the tongue after the obligatory prayers, related by Mujahid from Ibn 'Abbas. It is also related from Abu al-Ahwas that he said the same regarding all the glorification mentioned in these two verses.

Ibn Kathir paused with a *ya'*, Nafi' and Abu 'Amr paused without a *ya'*, and the rest paused and continued with a *ya'*. (Qira'at, the recognized variant readings of the Qur'an.) Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi said: the meaning is, "And listen to the account of the day the caller calls." The exegetes (mufassirun) said: the caller is Israfil, who stands on the rock of Bayt al-Maqdis and calls: "O people, come to the reckoning, for God commands you to gather for the judgment." This is the last blast (al-nafkha al-akhira). The "near place" is the rock of Bayt al-Maqdis. Ka'b and Muqatil said: it is the nearest point of the earth to the sky, eighteen miles away. Ibn al-Sa'ib said twelve miles. al-Zajjaj said: it is said that this rock is at the center of the earth.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿the day they hear the Shout in truth﴾, which is [this] second blast, ﴿in truth﴾, meaning the resurrection which there is no doubt about. ﴿That is the day of coming forth﴾ from the graves.

This is His saying: ﴿The day the earth splits open from them﴾. Ibn Kathir, Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read "tashsha ggaqu" with a doubled *shin*; the rest read it with a single *shin*. ﴿Swiftly﴾, meaning they come forth from it swiftly. ﴿That is a gathering easy for Us﴾, meaning effortless.

Then He consoled His Prophet, saying: ﴿We know best what they say﴾ in denying you, meaning the disbelievers of Makkah. ﴿And you are not over them a compeller (jabbar)﴾. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So remind by the Qur'an﴾, meaning admonish by it "whoever fears My warning (wa'id)." Ya'qub read "wa'idi" with a *ya'* in both states, meaning: what I threatened of punishment against whoever disobeys Me.
